rules.title: Policy document could not be parsed
rules.attack_unmapped_reason: Parser diagnostic about the input, not an adversary behavior.
rules.remediation: Fix the policy so it is valid IAM JSON (AWS itself rejects most of these documents); until then, paths that depend on it are not analyzed.

rules.title: Referenced policy or group is not in the snapshot
rules.attack_unmapped_reason: Parser diagnostic about the input, not an adversary behavior.
rules.remediation: Collect the snapshot again including AWS managed policies (get-account-authorization-details without filters); decisions that depend on the missing policy are conditional.

rules.title: Create a new default version of an attached policy
prerequisites: a customer managed policy is attached to the actor (directly or through a group)
rules.remediation: Remove iam:CreatePolicyVersion or scope it to policies that are not attached to the caller; deny it in a permissions boundary.

rules.title: Put an inline policy on its own role
prerequisites: the actor is a role allowed iam:PutRolePolicy on its own ARN
rules.remediation: Remove iam:PutRolePolicy from the role's policies, or scope its Resource to roles other than itself and add a permissions boundary that denies it.

rules.title: Put an inline policy on its own user
prerequisites: the actor is a user allowed iam:PutUserPolicy on its own ARN
rules.remediation: Remove iam:PutUserPolicy, or limit it with Resource and a permissions boundary so users cannot target themselves.

rules.title: Attach a managed policy to its own user
prerequisites: the actor is a user
rules.remediation: Remove the action from the principal's policies, scope its Resource to other entities, or add a permissions boundary that denies it. A condition on iam:PolicyARN can limit which policies may be attached.

rules.title: Attach a managed policy to its own role
prerequisites: the actor is a role
rules.remediation: Remove the action from the principal's policies, scope its Resource to other entities, or add a permissions boundary that denies it. A condition on iam:PolicyARN can limit which policies may be attached.

rules.title: Attach a managed policy to its own group
prerequisites: the actor is a member of the group
rules.remediation: Remove the action from the principal's policies, scope its Resource to other entities, or add a permissions boundary that denies it.

rules.title: Put an inline policy on its own group
prerequisites: the actor is a member of the group
rules.remediation: Remove the action from the principal's policies, scope its Resource to other entities, or add a permissions boundary that denies it.

rules.title: Add itself to a more privileged group
prerequisites: the actor is a user that is not yet a member
rules.remediation: Scope iam:AddUserToGroup to specific groups and never allow it on groups with administrative policies.

rules.title: Create an access key for another user
prerequisites: the target user has fewer than 2 access keys
rules.remediation: Scope iam:CreateAccessKey to the caller's own user (arn:aws:iam::<account>:user/${aws:username}).

rules.title: Rotate out and create an access key for another user
prerequisites: the target is an IAM user
rules.remediation: Scope iam:CreateAccessKey and iam:DeleteAccessKey to the caller's own user (arn:aws:iam::<account>:user/${aws:username}).

rules.title: Create a console password for another user
prerequisites: the target user has no console password yet
rules.remediation: Scope iam:CreateLoginProfile to the caller's own user and require MFA for console access.

rules.title: Change another user's console password
prerequisites: the target user has a console password
MFA on the target may still block console use
rules.remediation: Scope iam:UpdateLoginProfile to the caller's own user and enforce MFA for every console user.

rules.title: Rewrite a role's trust policy
prerequisites: the target role is not service-linked
the actor can assume the role once the trust names it
rules.remediation: Restrict iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy to administrators, scope it to specific role ARNs, or deny it in a permissions boundary.

rules.title: Assume a more privileged role
prerequisites: the role's trust policy accepts the actor (docs/research.md §2.4)

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Name only the principals that need the role in its trust policy, add conditions (sts:ExternalId, aws:PrincipalOrgID, MFA) and scope sts:AssumeRole in identity policies to specific role ARNs.

rules.title: Attach a policy to a role it can assume
prerequisites: the actor can already assume the role

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Remove the permission-management action on other principals, or deny it in a permissions boundary; also review how the caller can act as the target.

rules.title: Create a new policy version for a role it can assume
prerequisites: a customer managed policy is attached to the role
the actor can already assume the role

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Remove the permission-management action on other principals, or deny it in a permissions boundary; also review how the caller can act as the target.

rules.title: Put an inline policy on a role it can assume
prerequisites: the actor can already assume the role

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Remove the permission-management action on other principals, or deny it in a permissions boundary; also review how the caller can act as the target.

rules.title: Attach a policy to a user and create its access key
prerequisites: the actor can create credentials for the user
rules.remediation: Remove the permission-management action on other principals, or deny it in a permissions boundary; also review how the caller can act as the target.

rules.title: Put an inline policy on a user and create its access key
prerequisites: the actor can create credentials for the user
rules.remediation: Remove the permission-management action on other principals, or deny it in a permissions boundary; also review how the caller can act as the target.

rules.title: Modify a role's permissions and rewrite its trust
prerequisites: one of the permission actions plus iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on the role
rules.remediation: Remove the permission-management action on other principals, or deny it in a permissions boundary; also review how the caller can act as the target.

rules.title: Pass a role to a new EC2 instance
prerequisites: the role trusts ec2.amazonaws.com
the role is in an instance profile

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Scope iam:PassRole to the roles the caller must pass and add "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"iam:PassedToService": "ec2.amazonaws.com"}} only for those roles.

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Scope iam:PassRole to the roles the caller must pass and add "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"iam:PassedToService": "lambda.amazonaws.com"}} only for those roles.

rules.title: Update the code of an existing Lambda function and invoke it
prerequisites: a Lambda function runs with the role

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Restrict lambda:UpdateFunctionCode and lambda:InvokeFunction to the resources the caller owns; separate deployment roles from runtime roles.

rules.title: Run a command on an instance that has a role
prerequisites: an SSM-managed EC2 instance runs with the role

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Restrict ssm:SendCommand to the resources the caller owns; separate deployment roles from runtime roles.

rules.title: Start a build of an existing CodeBuild project
prerequisites: a CodeBuild project runs with the role

attack.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access

rules.remediation: Restrict codebuild:StartBuild to the resources the caller owns; separate deployment roles from runtime roles.

events.name: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
events.region: Global STS endpoint: us-east-1; regional STS endpoints: the endpoint's Region.
events.notes: Logged only in the role's account; userIdentity.type is WebIdentityUser.

blind_spots: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is a read-only event: write-only trails miss it.
The external side of the call is outside this account's trails.

prerequisites_unverified: a Lambda function runs with this role (no resource inventory)

events.name: Invoke
events.notes: Data event: not logged unless the trail enables Lambda data events.

events.name: UpdateFunctionCode20150331v2
events.notes: The event name carries a version suffix; ZipFile is omitted from the log.

blind_spots: Activity inside the compute resource is not logged; only later API calls made with the role appear (experimental).
Invoke is a data event: trails and event data stores do not log it by default, and Event history never shows it.
The new code itself is not in CloudTrail.

events.name: AssumeRole
events.region: Global STS endpoint: us-east-1; regional STS endpoints: the endpoint's Region.
events.notes: Logged in both accounts for cross-account calls, linked by sharedEventID; readOnly is true.

blind_spots: A denied cross-account AssumeRole is not logged in the target account.
AssumeRole is a read-only event: trails that keep only write management events miss it.
The external side of the call is outside this account's trails.

events.name: CreateFunction20150331
events.notes: The event name carries a version suffix; Environment and ZipFile are omitted from the log.

events.name: Invoke
events.notes: Data event: not logged unless the trail enables Lambda data events.

blind_spots: Activity inside the compute resource and credential reads from instance metadata or the runtime environment are not logged; only later API calls made with the role appear (experimental: inferred from the service documentation).
Invoke is a data event: trails and event data stores do not log it by default, and Event history never shows it.
The function code and environment variables are not in CloudTrail.
iam:PassRole is a permission, not an API call: it never appears as its own event. Look for the call that creates the resource, with the role in its request parameters.

events.name: AssumeRole
events.region: Global STS endpoint: us-east-1; regional STS endpoints: the endpoint's Region.
events.notes: Logged in both accounts for cross-account calls, linked by sharedEventID; readOnly is true.

blind_spots: A denied cross-account AssumeRole is not logged in the target account.
AssumeRole is a read-only event: trails that keep only write management events miss it.
The external side of the call is outside this account's trails.

findings.title: Pass a role to a new Lambda function and invoke it
findings.message: arn:aws:iam::111111111111:group/developers can act as arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/LambdaExecAdmin using iam:PassRole, lambda:CreateFunction, lambda:InvokeFunction
findings.remediation: Scope iam:PassRole to the roles the caller must pass and add "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"iam:PassedToService": "lambda.amazonaws.com"}} only for those roles.

findings.title: Update the code of an existing Lambda function and invoke it
findings.message: arn:aws:iam::111111111111:group/developers can act as arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/LambdaExecAdmin using lambda:InvokeFunction, lambda:UpdateFunctionCode (conditional; prerequisites not verified: a Lambda function runs with this role (no resource inventory))
findings.remediation: Restrict lambda:UpdateFunctionCode and lambda:InvokeFunction to the resources the caller owns; separate deployment roles from runtime roles.

findings.remediation: Fix the policy so it is valid IAM JSON (AWS itself rejects most of these documents); until then, paths that depend on it are not analyzed.
